claim: REGISTER ENTRY, as ruled: A CONTROL ANCHORED TO LIVE DATA SILENTLY RETIRES ITSELF THE MOMENT THE CORPUS IS FIXED. It passes today because the corpus currently matches it; when the defect is repaired the case becomes unreachable and the gate reports VACUOUS or, worse, PASS forever having checked nothing.
evidence: Occurred TWICE in gates written to enforce rules. gate3's named positive was the live attr-pn-review/primary divergence -- running --repair made it unreachable and the gate went VACUOUS. gate4's named positives were live kind-C and kind-D sites -- emptying kind D, the success the gate exists to produce, did the same.
rule: Controls must be anchored to a FIXTURE: synthetic, or pinned to an immutable object id. gate3 is now pinned to blob c623a213; gate4's are synthetic classifier probes.
note: this rule already existed in lessons.md and was violated inside gates built to enforce rules. Which is the argument for the gate, again.

claim: FOURTH shared-artefact collision of the night, and mine again -- within MINUTES of building the assertion for the third. I redirected gate output to /tmp/f1.txt and /tmp/f2.txt. /tmp is SHARED between lanes on this machine (the pre-push hook itself writes /tmp/durable_gate.log), and /tmp/f2.txt was another lane's artefact from 2026-08-26 (1,774 bytes, a Rekor/ancestry verification log). The shell's `>` truncated it to 0 the instant the second command started.
recovered: Fully and byte-for-byte, including mtime. I copied it to the session scratchpad BEFORE the truncation, having noticed the Aug-26 timestamp while polling; restored after killing the run. Verified: 1,774 bytes, identical head, mtime 2026-08-26.
why_it_matters: The residual limitation I had written into WHAT-REMAINS-DISCIPLINE minutes earlier -- 'the assertion covers out/ESCALATIONS.jsonl only; any other shared append-only artefact must be added by hand -- that list is discipline' -- fired immediately, on a DIFFERENT artefact in a DIFFERENT location. Generic filenames (f1, f2, a, tmp, out) in a shared scratch directory are a collision waiting to happen, and every lane picks the same names.
closed_by: NOTHING YET. This is a real, open gap.
next_step: Two candidates. (1) A lane-scoped scratch convention -- write to the session scratchpad, never /tmp -- enforced by a lint that refuses a redirect to a bare /tmp path in committed scripts. (2) Extend H.APPEND_ONLY thinking to a pre-run snapshot of any shared path a lane is about to write. (1) is cheaper and covers the actual failure.
rule: A SHARED SCRATCH DIRECTORY IS A SHARED ARTEFACT. The collision does not need an append-only log; it needs only two lanes choosing the same obvious filename, which is what obvious filenames are for.

claim: My Python edits wrote files in text mode on Windows, converting LF to CRLF. That rewrote EVERY LINE of three files including scripts/retire_2026_08_28.py -- a SHARED script -- producing a 174-line phantom diff in commit 335ae41f2 where the real change was ~55 lines. 22 files were affected.
detected_by: reading the commit's per-file --numstat and challenging an implausible number: +229/-174 for an addition of about 55 lines. Not by any gate.
fixed: all 22 files normalised back to LF in the following commit; scripts/retire_2026_08_28.py confirmed CRLF=0, matching what HEAD~1 held.
second_order: the normalisation SHRANK out/ESCALATIONS.jsonl by 24 bytes, and my own assert_append_only_intact FALSE-POSITIVED on it -- 27 records vs 27, but fewer bytes -- reporting 'a routine `>` destroyed another lane's records'. A false accusation, running in the direction of ACCUSING THE SUBJECT, which the blind-review report names as the dangerous direction because it reads as the check working.
closed_by: the assertion now counts RECORDS as the contract and compares bytes only after normalising line endings on both sides; a byte drop with the record count intact is a NOTE, not a finding. Re-proved both ways on the real file: 5-of-27 record loss -> FAIL; identical records rewritten as CRLF -> PASS; restored byte-identical.
rule: A CHECK'S OWN FALSE POSITIVE IS A FINDING ABOUT THE CHECK. Measure what the contract actually is -- for an append-only log that is RECORDS, never bytes -- because the convenient proxy is the one that fires on innocent changes.
